summary: myseliasan gains fleet configuration policy + drift detection: a FleetPolicy (fleet/site/node scope, per-node-kind) declares what a whitelisted set of node settings (recording continuity, camera reachability, tamper detection, appliance health thresholds, alert retention) ought to be, and a leader-gated background reconciler compares each adopted node's live settings against the winning policy every 15 minutes, reporting compliant/drifted/unknown/unmanaged per node. Enforcement — writing a drifted value back to the node over the existing control tunnel — is opt-in per policy and defaults off (report-only), with every enforced write audited. New superadmin-gated /api/fleet-policies* endpoints and a Fleet Policy screen. While building this, an unrelated backup gap was found and fixed: FleetRuleClause rows were never exported by the .selbackup 'rules' section, so a restored fleet correlation rule always came back with zero clauses and could never fire; a new 'policies' backup section covers the new entities and the 'rules' section now carries clauses too.
compatibility: No policies exist until an operator creates one, so an upgraded install reports every node 'unmanaged' with zero behavior change until a policy is authored; Enforce defaults to false on every new policy, so even an authored policy only reports drift and writes nothing to a node unless an operator deliberately turns enforcement on. New DB tables (fleet_policy, fleet_policy_item) are additive via the normal auto-migrator, no manual migration needed. Existing .selbackup files made before this change restore normally (missing 'policies' section is skipped, and older exports still lacking clauses restore rules with no clauses, same as before this fix); new exports include both. Half-benched: the reconciler has been exercised against a REAL mymatasan node (all 21 governable fields verified to exist, to be settable, and to survive a merge without disturbing the ungoverned fields in the same section; report-only confirmed to write nothing; an unreachable node confirmed to report 'unknown' rather than 'compliant'). Not yet exercised over the mTLS control channel with an adopted fleet, nor through the API/UI — see docs/FLAGSHIP_HARDENING_PLAN.md W2-1 and docs/FLAGSHIP_BENCH_CHECKLIST.md.
